{"action":"shell","command":"cd /testbed && cat > HANDOFF.md << 'EOF'\n# Milestone 1 handoff: tinydb.journal.BatchWriter\n\n## Implemented\n- `tinydb/journal.py`: `BatchWriter(db)` wrapping a TinyDB instance; `apply(operations)` on the default table only.
  - R01: `{'op':'insert','document':mapping}` -> returns inserted IDs; `{'op':'remove','doc_id':positive int}` -> no result; `[]` -> `[]`; unknown/malformed ops (incl. non-mapping ops, missing keys, non-positive/non-int doc_id, bools, non-iterable input) raise ValueError.
  - R02: atomic. Deep-copied snapshot of `db.storage.read()` taken before applying; on any error `storage.write(snapshot)` restores exact pre-batch state (MemoryStorage returns its live dict, so a deep copy is required). Also resets the table's `_next_id` counter and query cache so previously acquired `db.table('_default')` handles reflect both success and rollback, and ID sequencing continues correctly.
  - R03: documents are deep-copied on insert (no aliasing of caller input; post-apply mutation cannot touch DB). Ordinary TinyDB APIs untouched.
  - Note: `Table._read_table()`/`get()` use string keys (JSON-style), so existence checks must go through `table.get(doc_id=...)` rather than raw dict membership.
- `tests/test_journal.py`: 42 tests (memory + JSONStorage params) covering R01/R02/R03, rollback visibility through preexisting handles, other-table preservation, ID sequencing after rollback, generator input.

## Verified
- `python -m pytest -o addopts= -q` -> 265 passed (223 upstream + 42 journal).
- `python -m pytest -o addopts= acceptance_public.py -q` -> 2 passed.
- Upstream tests and sources unchanged (only new files added).
- Note: repo `pytest.ini` addopts require pytest-cov which is not installed here; run with `-o addopts=`.
EOF\necho done; ls HANDOFF.md"}
